crossing supervisor Listen Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print Content components School crossing supervisors have a much-valued role in Boroondara. On an average school day in Boroondara, they help 9,266 pedestrians to cross the street while 74,426 motor vehicles use our roads during school crossing times. We are always looking for school crossing supervisors. If you are friendly, reliable and flexible, this role is for you. What does a school crossing supervisor do? This paid position gives you the opportunity to get involved in your community and improve road safety for children, people with a disability and the general public who use our 114 school crossings. School crossing supervisors: • work part-time Monday to Friday, from 8 am to 9 am and from 3 pm to 4 pm, during the school term • play an important role in educating children with ‘Stop, Look and Listen’ instructions • are responsible for reporting any road hazards or potential risks • help to encourage active and independent travel. About you We are looking for people aged 18 and older who: • can attend shifts at short notice • have their own reliable transport • are able to work across several locations • can complete the pre-employment medical and police checks. You will have access to a full training program before starting your role. Submit an online application through our Careers website . Attend an interview – meet with one of our Council Officers at Council, located at 8 Inglesby Road in Camberwell. Provide us with relevant employment documents – including your Working With Children Check, Police Check and evidence of your COVID-19 vaccination status. Complete a medical assessment. Apply to become a School Crossings Supervisor We are always recruiting new school crossing supervisors to help people to cross our roads safely at peak school times. You’ll use your creativity, multimedia capabilities and communications skills to help us inform, engage and support our community. A little bit about the role The Digital Marketing Officer supports the Strategic Communications department to ensure Council’s digital marketing activities are effective, and Council’s social media and email newsletters are driving positive community outcomes. This role reports to the Digital Marketing Lead and works with internal stakeholders across Council to deliver campaigns, produce platform appropriate multimedia content and use performance insights to continually improve Council’s digital communications. The Digital Marketing Officer plays an integral role in helping Council connect with the community through timely, accessible and engaging content. Key responsibilities include: Plan and produce platform appropriate content, including video, photography and written content for social media and email newsletters. Work with internal partners to deliver digital marketing campaigns that are informed by customer insights, data, market trends and best-practice approaches. Write, edit and publish accessible digital content that provides a positive customer experience. Maintain publishing schedules and ensure Council’s digital channels remain active, timely and aligned with community interests. Monitor and moderate community interactions across digital channels in line with Council policies and agreed processes. Use analytics and reporting to measure performance, identify trends and recommend improvements. Manage digital marketing activity (paid and organic), including campaign setup, audience targeting, budget monitoring and performance optimisation. Provide digital communications advice, training and input to support continuous improvement across Council A little bit about you You will have proven ability to engage and grow audiences on social media, underpinned by a deep knowledge of social media platforms, contemporary content approaches, creative trends and audience behaviour. You have demonstrated experience producing multimedia content for social media and email newsletter audiences reflecting platform specific aesthetics and viewer preferences. You will have demonstrated experience working in a multi-stakeholder environment developing marketing strategies and delivering digital marketing campaigns. You will be a confident communicator with strong writing skills and the ability to build effective relationships throughout the organisation. You will have the ability to use digital analytics to gather information and identify insights and moderate digital channels and manage online community interactions to deliver the best possible customer outcomes. You will also bring tertiary qualifications in marketing, media, communications or a related discipline, or relevant professional experience in a similar role. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Local Laws Officer (15170) Requisition ID 15170 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Local Laws Officer Join a dynamic, investigations team that supports each other to succeed Deliver meaningful outcomes to the community in safety and amenity $93,845 - $101,184 per annum (plus Super) Tool of trade vehicle provided (non-hybrid position) Join us in building a professional investigations team and help deliver a responsive, community-focused Local Laws service. In this role, you will contribute to a safe, liveable and well-maintained municipality while providing high-quality regulatory service to residents and stakeholders. About the role At City of Boroondara, our Local Laws directly contributes to our purpose of protecting the health, safety, amenity and assets of the municipality. Based within the large and busy department of Civic Services, the team works as part of five field-based teams and many others within the Urban Living Directorate. You will respond to reported breaches of the Amenity Local Law and the Environment Protection Act, using education, investigation and enforcement to achieve compliance. The role involves managing a varied caseload, gathering evidence, preparing clear records and working within established procedures to resolve matters fairly and effectively. The position includes investigating issues such as illegally dumped rubbish under the EPA, unsightly properties, overhanging vegetation, illegally advertising and the occupation of Council land, while providing courteous and timely service to community members. From time to time, you will also support the Animal Management team with park patrols, and work with external stakeholders including Victoria Police, the Magistrates’ Court and Council prosecutors. You will work an average of 42-hours per week over a four week roster cycle and rotating weekend work is required every 4 weeks with penalty rates that convert into an annualised salary. This is a non-hybrid role as our ‘office’ is in the community, every day and our success comes from working together with other officers, as a team! About you We are looking for someone who brings sound judgement, a strong customer focus and a collaborative approach. You will be supported to build your knowledge and succeed in the role. You will have experience delivering customer service in a complex regulatory environment or another fast-paced setting, with the ability to communicate clearly, build rapport and respond professionally in a range of situations under pressure. Experience in areas such as retail, hospitality, community services or other enforcement role can provide a strong foundation for success in this role. You will be able to investigate issues methodically, collect information accurately and prepare clear notes and reports. Knowledge of compliance, local laws or related legislation will be well regarded, as will the ability to interpret policy and apply it in practical situations. If you are still developing in these areas, a willingness to learn will be equally valued. Success in this role also requires respectful negotiation skills, sound problem-solving and judgement skills, de-escalating interpersonal situations with members of the community, and the capacity to work across the community each day, including walking for extended periods and assisting with animal handling when required. A qualification in enforcement, local laws, justice or a related field is desirable, but not essential. Want to know more? Please refer to the Position description What sets us apart? An investment in your ongoing professional and personal development. You will be part of a team that makes a real difference. Working at Boroondara means contributing to creating positive change in the world. Join us in a role where your work matters, and you contribute to meaningful outcomes. A supportive and friendly workplace culture that values diversity, collaboration and continuous improvement. We offer many staff benefits such as study support, wellbeing programs, gym and pool memberships. Employment requirements Applicants must have the right to work in Australia and hold a valid Woking With Children Check. Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check. Preferred applicants will also be required to undertake a pre-employment medical assessment. How to Apply Follow these steps, carefully: Please submit your application online via the ‘ Apply ’ button by Thursday 6 August 2026 11:59pm . Ensure you address your cover letter to Natasha Curmi and answer the following questions: What about the Local Laws Officer role motivates you? Why is this the next logical step in your career? All applications must be made via the online portal; no applications direct to the hiring manager will be considered. No calls or applications from agencies please. For any confidential discussion please contact Natasha Curmi, Team Leader Compliance (during business hours) on 0459 854 662 . We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. closing_text: PAGE 1 Position Description IMMUNISATION NURSE Created 15/05/2026 Alpine Shire Council’s Values - ICARE Innovation | Collaboration | Accountability | Respect | Empowerment Our shared values and behaviours are integral to how we go about our work, interact with each other and our community. Child Safety Commitment at Alpine Shire Council Alpine Shire Council is committed to being a child safe organisation. Every child and young person has the right to feel safe. All our employees have a shared responsibility to protect children and young people from harm and abuse. Alpine Shire Council have established policies, procedures and training to achieve these commitments. Diversity & Inclusivity at Alpine Shire Council Alpine Shire Council is an Equal Opportunity employer. We value people of all abilities, people from culturally and/or linguistically diverse backgrounds and First Nations peoples. We are committed to upholding a safe, inclusive and respectful workplace that values the contribution of all. POSITION OVERVIEW The immunisations team work to promote and maintain high standards of public health and wellbeing within our community, with a focus on disease and illness prevention. You will provide an efficient, responsive and responsible service. You will be required to promote the Alpine Shire Council as a customer-focused organisation at all times. You will undertake key responsibilities in a professional, efficient and timely manner, and contribute to Council’s aim of being a high performing organisation. You will need to be passionate and multi-skilled and able to consistently deliver at high standard operational services in a tidy, organised, caring and safe environment. You will contribute towards the public health agenda by improving health outcomes for our children, young people and our community. CLASSIFICATION AND RELATIONSHIPS Classification: Nurses (ANF –Victorian Local Government Award 2015) varied by the Alpine Shire Council Enterprise Agreement 2023. Reports to: Maternal and Child Health Nurse Coordinator. Supervises: Nil KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Accountability and extent of authority • Accountable to direct supervisor and manager. • Duties performed within Council policies and procedures. • Duties to be performed within specified timeframes. • Authority to liaise with internal and external customers to ensure accurate and up to date information is maintained in a timely manner. Immunisations • Administer vaccines at immunisation sessions as required and in accordance with the National Immunisation Program requirements and National Immunisations Framework for Health Professionals. • Assist to ensure accurate recording of all relevant client information. • Ensure the confidentiality of client information is maintained as required. • Ensure the safe keeping of materials and equipment. • Equipment and resources are managed effectively to reduce waste and promote cost efficiency. • Provide assistance with determining an efficient annual schedule of immunisations for Alpine Shire, including: immunisations for 0-5 year old children, the secondary school program, Council staff and older eligible adult influenza vaccine sessions. • Maintain a constant drive towards service improvement. Other duties • Ensure all processing and tasks undertaken are efficient. • Display a punctual, reliable and positive approach to work. • Continually review and improve work methods associated with this role. • Undertake other duties as directed by the manager or supervisor. • In addition to the responsibilities described in this document, all employees must comply with the Alpine Shire Council’s Code of Conduct and Corporate Policies. Judgement and decision making • Guidance is always available from immediate supervisor or manager • The particular tasks to be performed may involve selection from a • limited range of existing techniques, systems, equipment, methods or processes in a defined range of recurring work situations. Management skills • Ability to manage your time and plan your day to achieve specific and set objectives. Interpersonal skills • Good oral and written communication skills with customers, other employees and members of the public and in the resolution of minor problems. • Display a punctual, reliable and positive approach to work • Ability to project a positive image in communicating with both internal and external customers at all times EXPERTISE Essential Qualifications • Victorian driver licence. • Current and valid nursing registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation (AHPRA). • Authorised Immunisation provider. • Working with Children Check. Experience • Previous experience in delivering immunisations and good working knowledge about the National Immunisation Program. Specialist Skills and Knowledge • Understanding of the role including relevant frameworks and guidelines. • Undertaking any personal development as required of registrations and/or as changes are required of the National Immunisation Program. • Sound written and verbal communication skills. • Keen interest and knowledge of vaccine preventable diseases of public health significance and immunisation. • Capacity to prioritise, organise individual work plan and to work semi- autonomously. • Capacity to communicate confidently and independently with senior health professionals and members of the public. HEALTH, SAFETY AND RISK DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Nothing is more important than the health and safety of yourself and those around you. You must: • Perform all tasks in a manner that does not place at risk the health and safety of any person. • Seek assistance when unsure of how to perform a task. • Ensure you observe, understand and comply with all Occupational Health and Safety Legislation, Regulations, Codes of Practice, Policies, Procedures and directives. • Regularly inspect your work environment for hazards. • Immediately report all workplace incidents, accidents, near-misses and hazards to a supervisor. • Support the return-to-work plan for any injured worker when returning to work. • Council Employees do not smoke in any workplace or when engaged in work related activities. Smoking is an issue for both Council and employees as it impacts on both the work and personal life of the smoker and other employees and in some cases the reputation of the Council. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS Daily work will be performed in an outdoor environment, as such: • You will be exposed to those conditions normally encountered in an indoor Environment. • Physical demands are moderate to strenuous, consisting of the ability to sit, stand, stoop, reach, bend, climb, lift and pull using safe manual handling practices. • • You must be able to see and hear in the normal range, with or without correction, and communicate well both verbally and in written form, and must be able to be understood. • You must have the stamina to work long hours, if assigned, and must be willing to work an irregular schedule, which may include weekends, holidays, evenings, and/or varying shifts. • The work environment may include uneven surfaces and up and down stairs.
